scenarios.name: Stagflationary Re-emergence
scenarios.description: Supply chain disruptions from geopolitical conflicts drive energy and commodity prices higher, while slowing industrial production and employment fail to catch up, leading to stickier inflation despite high interest rates.

impacts.explanation: Supply shocks increase cost-push inflation pressures.
Higher costs and rates dampen consumer spending and industrial output.

scenarios.reasoning: Using base rates for stagflationary cycles and adjusting for current high trade deficits and rising debt-to-GDP ratios.
tetlockPillars: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem
tetlockCommandments: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem

scenarios.name: Soft Landing Consolidation
scenarios.description: Inflation continues its descent toward 2% target through demand cooling, while the Fed successfully navigates a pivot to neutral, supporting steady but modest growth and low unemployment.

impacts.explanation: Moderating economy leads to slight cooling in the labor market.
Stable consumption and moderate growth continue.

scenarios.reasoning: Granular analysis of current low unemployment and cooling inflation suggests a continued convergence toward the target without a crash.
tetlockCommandments: Strike the right balance between under- and overreacting to evidence

scenarios.name: Trade Protectionism Surge
scenarios.description: Increased trade wars and tariffs aimed at decoupling supply chains lead to higher costs for imported goods and a widening trade deficit, impacting retail and industrial sectors.

impacts.explanation: Tariffs and supply chain shifts increase the value of imports/decreases competitiveness.
Higher prices for consumer goods dampen discretionary spending.

scenarios.reasoning: Geopolitical tensions regarding trade alliances and tariffs act as a clashing force against consumer spending capacity.
tetlockPillars: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem
tetlockCommandments: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem

scenarios.name: Credit Crunch/Debt Crisis
scenarios.description: Rising 10-year Treasury yields and high federal debt levels increase the cost of servicing national debt and private debt, leading to reduced investment and credit tightening.

impacts.explanation: Rising risk premium and fiscal deficits push yields higher.
Higher yields translate to higher mortgage rates, cooling new construction.

scenarios.reasoning: Extrapolating current debt trends and yield movements suggests a tail risk of fiscal-driven tightening.
tetlockCommandments: Break seemingly intractable problems into tractable sub-problems

scenarios.name: Technological Productivity Boom
scenarios.description: Rapid integration of AI and automation boosts industrial productivity and services, offsetting labor cost pressures and driving GDP growth higher than current trends.

impacts.explanation: Automation increases efficiency and output levels.
Productivity gains drive higher real output per hour worked.

scenarios.reasoning: Aggregating recent tech sector trends with historical productivity cycles.
tetlockCommandments: Bring out the best in others and let others bring out the best in you

methodology: Applied Tetlock's probabilistic approach by establishing a base rate for economic cycles (Soft Landing) and then adjusting for specific clashing forces: geopolitical supply shocks, trade protectionism, and technological productivity gains. Sub-problems were identified via granular indicator analysis.
geopoliticalSummary: Tensions in trade alliances and potential supply chain weaponization pose risks to inflation and trade balances.
geoeconomicSummary: The widening trade deficit and rising yields suggest a shifting global capital flow that complicates domestic fiscal policy.
currentEventsSummary: Focus on the interplay between high federal debt levels and the transition toward a lower-interest-rate environment.
